paragraphs.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 (DEE46) is a severe neurologic disorder characterized by severe developmental delay and intractable seizures that are refractory to conventional antiepileptic medications. Status epilepticus may occur (Li et al., 2016; Tsuchida et al., 2018).

paragraphs.text: In 2 unrelated children with DEE46, Li et al. (2016) used exome and candidate panel sequencing to identify a recurrent de novo heterozygous missense mutation in the GRIN2D gene (c.1999G-A; val667-to-ile, V667I). The mutation lies in the M3 transmembrane domain, which is involved in channel gating. In functional studies, V667I was a gain-of-function mutation: it doubled glutamate and glycine potency, increased channel open probability 6-fold, reduced receptor sensitivity to endogenous negative modulators such as extracellular protons, and prolonged deactivation after glutamate removal.

paragraphs.text: In 3 unrelated patients with DEE46, Tsuchida et al. (2018) used whole-exome sequencing to identify novel heterozygous missense variants in the GRIN2D gene. All of the altered residues were highly conserved across vertebrates and among the 4 GluN2 subunits. Structural analysis suggested that all 3 variants probably impair GluN2D function, either by affecting intersubunit interaction or by altering channel gating activity.

paragraphs.text: Li et al. (2016) found that the mutant NMDA receptors were sensitive to FDA-approved NMDA receptor antagonists and treated both of their patients with oral memantine, which resulted in mild to moderate improvement in seizure burden and development. The older proband later developed refractory status epilepticus, which improved dramatically on electroclinical measures with ketamine and magnesium. The authors suggested that NMDA receptor antagonists may be useful as adjuvant therapy in individuals with GRIN2D gain-of-function mutations.

paragraphs.text: In 2 unrelated children with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-46 (DEE46), Li et al. (2016) found a recurrent de novo heterozygous c.1999G-A transition in the GRIN2D gene, resulting in a val667-to-ile (V667I) substitution in the M3 transmembrane domain, which is involved in channel gating. They found the mutation by exome and candidate panel sequencing. Functional studies showed a gain-of-function effect: the mutation doubled glutamate and glycine potency, increased channel open probability 6-fold, reduced sensitivity to endogenous negative modulators such as extracellular protons, and prolonged deactivation after glutamate removal. Cultured neurons transfected with the mutant cDNA showed dendritic swelling and cell death, which the authors suggested reflected excitotoxicity. The mutant receptors were sensitive to FDA-approved NMDA receptor antagonists, and treating both patients with memantine led to mild to moderate improvement.
